name: desert
description: What grows where there is no water: cacti, succulents and dry scrub. TWO HANDS IN ONE PACK, from two sheets, and they do not mix well in a single scene. The 25 with plant names — `saguaro`, `ocotillo`, `prickly-pear` and so on — are finely drawn, closer to botanical illustration. The 25 with shape names — `round-barrel`, `twin-column`, `paddle-cactus` — are flat torn paper, and those are the ones that sit with the rest of the troupe. Pick from one set or the other.
stylePrompt:
STYLE — follow this exactly, it matters more than the subject: Torn and cut paper collage. Every single shape is a piece of coloured paper that has been cut with scissors or torn by hand and laid flat on top of the others, with visible torn deckle edges, paper grain, fibre and a dry speckled gouache texture inside each shape. Small details — faces, eyes, twigs, stitching — are drawn on top in fine black ink line. Seen STRAIGHT ON, flat, from the front — the way an audience sees a puppet theatre or a paper cut-out stage. There is no vanishing point and no perspective anywhere. Depth is made only by putting one flat shape in front of another, never by making things smaller as they go back. ABSOLUTELY NOT: digital painting, watercolour, gouache painting, concept art, rendered 3D, airbrushing, photorealism, cinematic lighting, volumetric light, glow, ambient occlusion, depth of field, blur, gradients, soft shading, cast shadows, reflections, perspective depth, or texture that looks painted rather than papery. Nothing is lit. Nothing is round. Nothing recedes. Everything is flat. Shapes are simple, geometric and slightly naive — built from a few pieces, the way a child's paper cut-out is. Palette: muted, warm and mid-century — moss and olive green, deep navy used instead of black, brick red, cream, dusty rose, mustard, soft pink. Four to six colours in total, used as large flat areas.

The sheet is about: desert plants — cacti, succulents, and the scrub that grows where there is no water. Everything on it belongs to that one subject.

Draw ONE sheet: a 5 × 5 grid of 25 separate pictures. Each cell is 1:1 — square. The cells must be exactly equal in size and evenly spaced, filling the whole image edge to edge, in reading order. Leave a clear even gap between cells and keep every subject well inside its own cell — nothing may touch or cross a cell edge. No grid lines, no borders, no numbers, no captions, no text, no watermark. NO WHITE OUTLINES. Do not draw a white keyline, a die-cut sticker border, a stroke or a glow around anything. This is not a sticker pack. NO OUTLINES. Before you draw anything, write out all 25 descriptions and check them: every one must be a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT object, not a variation of its neighbour. 25 genuinely different things, or the sheet is wasted.

Each cell holds ONE piece of scenery on a PLAIN WHITE background, cut-out style, with no shadow, no ground under it, no sky behind it and nothing else in the cell. Draw the whole object, not a part of a scene, and do not draw two things in one cell. Keep the same scale, the same lighting and the same level of detail across every cell.

Then cut it up at https://fastcut.needle.tools: fastcut_add_image, fastcut_set_output_format (WebP), fastcut_split_sprites, fastcut_download as a ZIP.

saguaro.description: the tall branching cactus everyone pictures — the tallest piece here, and the one that reads as desert on its own

organ-pipe.description: a cluster of straight ribbed columns, as tall as the saguaro but denser

joshua-tree.description: a shaggy forked trunk with spiked crowns — the only piece here shaped like a tree

ocotillo.description: tall whip-like canes tipped with red flowers, narrow and see-through

prickly-pear.description: flat spined pads stacked into a clump

golden-barrel.description: a fat ribbed mustard globe — the brightest thing here

old-man-cactus.description: two shaggy pale columns, hairy enough to look like a joke

crested-cactus.description: a fan-shaped mutated cactus, wider than it is tall

bishops-cap.description: a low star-sectioned cactus, seen from above

flowering-cactus.description: a small pad cactus with one pink bloom

agave.description: a broad rosette of grey-green blades — softer and paler than stones-and-plants/agave

yucca.description: a spiked rosette carrying a cream flower spike — the flowering one; stones-and-plants/yucca is bare

desert-spoon.description: a fine-bladed grey rosette, spraying outward

aloe.description: speckled leaves under a red flower spike

echeveria.description: a pink succulent rosette, low and round

jade.description: a small tree of round green leaves on a brown stem

ice-plant.description: a low mat of leaves scattered with pink daisies

desert-rose.description: a swollen red trunk topped with pink blossom — the strangest shape in the pack

brittlebrush.description: a sprawling grey shrub dotted with yellow

creosote.description: a wiry open shrub with small round leaves

sagebrush.description: a pale silver-green bush, the softest silhouette here

pointed-rosette.description: a spray of narrow pointed blades

simple-yucca.description: blades around a cream flower spike

star-cactus.description: five rounded arms from a centre, seen from above

round-barrel.description: a mustard globe with pale ribs — the brightest piece here

five-stem-ocotillo.description: five stems tipped with pink buds
